title: Ring augmented Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass vs non banded standard Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass within BMI range of 35 to 55 kg/m²
summary:
Roux-en-Y gastric bypass is a recognized surgical procedure for treating severe obesity. It involves reducing the size of the stomach and altering the digestive tract. This method usually leads to long-term weight loss and can also improve metabolism, for example in cases of diabetes. Over time, however, the small portion of the stomach may expand again. This can reduce the feeling of satiety, which can lead to weight gain or unpleasant symptoms after eating. A possible further development is gastric bypass with an additional ring. This ring is designed to prevent the stomach from expanding again, thus stabilizing weight loss. It could also help to improve comorbidities such as diabetes more effectively. However, the ring itself can cause problems, such as vomiting, slipping, or growing into the tissue. Little research has been done on how the ring affects heartburn or typical discomfort after eating. 
This study therefore compares two groups of severely obese patients: one with gastric bypass surgery with a ring and one without a ring. The participants will be observed over several years. The most important question is how much weight they have lost after five years. The study will also examine whether comorbidities such as diabetes improve, what the quality of life is like, and whether symptoms such as discomfort after eating or heartburn occur. 
A total of around 2,000 people are expected to take part. Initial indications suggest that gastric bypass surgery with a ring could lead to greater weight loss. The study will now clarify whether it also has long-term benefits for health and quality of life.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
BMI ≥35kg/m2 plus comorbidities or BMI ≥40kg/m2 to BMI ≤55 kg/m2
Exclusion criteria:
• any chronic inflammatory or malignant disease
• any previous bariatric surgery
• type 1 diabetes
• peptic ulcer
• contraindication for general anaesthesia
• drug or alcohol abuse
• untreated thyroid dysfunction
• pregnancy or breast-feeding woman
• expected non-compliance
• participation in another interventional trial requiring insurance
• Oesophageal Varices
• Advanced Liver cirrhosis
• Vulnerable persons according to the law
• Allergy to silicone
